title: Anthropic launches Opus 5
author: Modelverse Editorial
excerpt: Opus 5 will be both cheaper and less restrictive than Fable, likely making it preferable in most use cases.
body:
Anthropic unveiled Opus 5, the latest addition to its flagship series, positioning it as a more affordable and less constrained alternative to the larger Fable 5 model. Released just two months after Opus 4.8, Opus 5 joins the recent wave of 5‑series models that includes Mythos 5, Sonnet 5 and Fable 5, leaving only the Haiku variant awaiting its upgrade. The company highlighted that Opus 5 excels at self‑checking and iterative refinement, demonstrated by its ability to construct a complete computer‑vision pipeline from an incomplete prompt in internal tests.  

Unlike Fable 5, Opus 5 is not bound by the 30‑day data‑retention rule that applies to Fable and Mythos, addressing privacy concerns while still retaining safeguards against malicious cybersecurity uses such as binary vulnerability scanning. The model’s safety classifiers are triggered far less often—about 85 % less frequently—than those for Fable 5, and a new beta feature called Automatic Fallbacks lets users route flagged requests to a weaker model instead of receiving an error, preserving API continuity.  

For developers and researchers, Opus 5 offers a compelling mix of performance, cost efficiency, and flexible safety controls, making it suitable for a broad range of applications where the heavier Fable 5 would be overkill. Its availability now fills a gap in Anthropic’s lineup and signals the company’s strategy of tiered models that balance capability with usability.
